## Posts

### OpenNote: Private, Local-First AI Study Tool for Your Documents

- URL: https://blogs.ramratan.in/opennote/
- Published: 2026-09-25
- Updated: 2026-10-15

OpenNote is a privacy-focused open source answer to Google's NotebookLM. Instead
of binding education to one model and one prompt, it takes the opposite
approach. It's a terminal-based study companion that turns the reader's own
PDFs, documents, web pages, and notes into a private, searchable knowledge base
that works with every major LLM provider available.

OpenNote reads the reader's files directly rather than chatting with a general
LLM whose answers drift beyond the source material. It organizes PDFs, office
documents, and saved web pages into a local library, and when asked a question
it finds the exact passages in the user's own material that answer it, then
builds its response strictly from what it found there. Every answer comes with a
citation pointing back to the specific source passage it was drawn from, and if
the answer is not in the documents, OpenNote says so instead of inventing one.

Because everything is processed and stored locally, notes, textbooks, and
research stay private by default. There is no upload step, no cloud storage of
the user's files, and nothing sitting on a third-party server. The user brings
their own AI provider key, whether that is OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, or
another provider, and OpenNote uses it only to generate answers, never to store
documents.

Beyond question and answer, OpenNote can turn source material into study
artifacts: mind maps, study guides, FAQ sheets, topic briefings, timelines, and
narrated audio or short slideshow videos summarizing a topic. If the setup does
not support audio or video generation, it falls back to a clean written version
rather than failing.

OpenNote does not lock users into one provider. It is bring-your-own-key with
support for five-plus providers, and any `/v1/models`-compatible endpoint can be
pointed at it, so a fully offline local model can be used instead. Users without
the hardware for that can run a free Colab or Kaggle notebook and point OpenNote
at it.

The interface is a terminal with dedicated modes for asking questions, searching
the library, and generating study materials, plus a live context meter showing
exactly how much of the model's context window is filled, how many tokens have
been used, and what it is costing.

- Repository: https://github.com/natarmr/opennote
- Installer: `curl -fsSL https://ramratan.in/install | bash`
